::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Novr 8th 1864  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Westcountry Studies Library, Exeter/ Yonge 1864/ 7
:::

My dear [Miss Smith](people/person_263.qmd)
I so seldom see the paper that I did not know that this greatest sorrow that can befall one’s unmarried life had come upon you.[^1] It takes me back at once to ten years ago when I was tasting the same cup, and strangely enough there was the same connection between the sorrow and my first real [success](cmy_books/cmybook_15.qmd). How you must feel the change & the sorrow for others as well as yourself. I am glad there is not in your case the shock of an immediate break of home, but that you have time to detach yourself gradually. As to the grief itself, I think it is one that lives more than any other I have known and yet is more precious. And those testimonies from poor neighbours do so live with one like treasures through the rest of ones life.

The [Anastasias](other_books/otherbook_361.qmd) must I am sure be a success from the tone of all the notices I have seen of them, and [Miss Taylor](people/person_1397.qmd) is very much pleased with them, you know she is a great admirer of yours (except [the Websters](other_books/otherbook_275.qmd)) but she has not guessed you here. She likes the 3d volume specially. I am just going to enjoy it

With many thanks
yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Envelope addressed to Miss Smith/ 8 Wellington Road/ Charlton/ SE postmarked Winchester 8 November 1864 and London SE 9 November 1864.
[^2]: The Rev. [Richard Carter Smith](people/person_297.qmd) died on 1 October 1864.  CMY's father [WCY](people/person_1631.qmd) had died in 1853.
